items.text: Function: The A-not-A form of making a question is the most neutral way to ask a question in Chinese and closest to yes/no questions in English.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 王先生要不要喝咖啡？
items.py: Wáng Xiānshēng yào bú yào hē kāfēi?
items.en: Does Mr. Wang want to have some coffee?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 這是不是烏龍茶？
items.py: Zhè shì bú shì Wūlóng chá?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 臺灣人喜歡不喜歡喝茶？
items.py: Táiwān rén xǐhuān bù xǐhuān hē chá?
items.en: Do Taiwanese people like to drink tea?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Structures: The “A” in the structure refers to the first verbal element.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他喝咖啡。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他喝不喝咖啡？
items.en: Does he want to drink coffee?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你是日本人。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你是不是日本人？
items.py: Nǐ shì bú shì Rìběn rén?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他來臺灣。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他來不來臺灣？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Usage: When the verbal element in an A-not-A question is disyllabic (XY), the second syllable (Y) can be dropped in the first “A” of the pattern, so “XY-not-XY” is the same as “X-not-XY”. For example, 你喜歡不喜歡我？ Nǐ xǐhuān bù xǐhuān wǒ? is the same as 你喜不喜歡我？ Nǐ xǐ bù xǐhuān wǒ? (Do you like me?)

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Function: Questions can be formed using the question particle 嗎 ma. It is usually used for short questions.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你好嗎？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你來接我們嗎？
items.en: Are you here to pick us up?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他是日本人嗎？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Structures: SENTENCE + 嗎 ma? The sentence in 嗎 ma questions can be either in the affirmative or negative.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他不姓陳嗎？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你不是臺灣人嗎？
items.py: Nǐ bú shì Táiwān rén ma?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他不喝咖啡嗎？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Usage: The A-not-A question form indicates no assumption, and is used for neutral inquiries or longer inquiries. It does not take a 嗎 ma question particle at the end of the sentence. One cannot say *這是不是茶嗎？ Zhè shì bú shì chá ma? (‘Is this tea?’). 嗎 ma questions, by contrast, are used for short inquiries. But in most cases, these two forms of question are often interchangeable.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你好嗎？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你要喝茶嗎？
items.en: Do you want to drink tea?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！

items.text: In Chinese, short answers in the affirmative can be made by simply repeating the verb from the question.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！

items.text: 他喜歡不喜歡喝茶？
items.py: Tā xǐhuān bù xǐhuān hē chá?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 喜歡。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Negative replies can be formed by repeating the main verb in its negative form, i.e., 不 bù + verb, followed by a sentence in the negative. 不 bù is an adverb which is placed before a verb or another adverb, e.g.,

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他是不是李先生？
items.py: Tā shì bú shì Lǐ Xiānshēng?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 不是，他不是李先生。
items.py: Bú shì, tā bú shì Lǐ Xiānshēng.
items.en: No, he is not Mr. Li.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 王先生喝茶嗎？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 不，他不喝。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 李小姐是不是臺灣人？
items.py: Lǐ Xiǎojiě shì bú shì Táiwān rén?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 不是，李小姐不是臺灣人。
items.py: Bú shì, Lǐ Xiǎojiě bú shì Táiwān rén.
items.en: No, Miss Li is not Taiwanese.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: In Chinese, the answer to a question can consist of just the verb in the question asked.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他要不要喝咖啡？
items.py: Tā yào bú yào hē kāfēi?
items.en: Does he want to drink coffee?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 不要。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 你喜歡不喜歡喝烏龍茶？
items.py: Nǐ xǐhuān bù xǐhuān hē Wūlóng chá?
items.en: Do you like to drink Oolong tea?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 不喜歡。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 陳小姐是不是美國人？
items.py: Chén Xiǎojiě shì bú shì Měiguó rén?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 不是。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Usage: There are some exceptions to the rules above. For example, when the verb is 姓 xìng “to be surnamed” or 叫 jiào “to be called”. When the question is 他姓李嗎？ Tā xìng Lǐ ma? ‘Is he surnamed Li?’, the negative reply should be 不姓李 Bú xìng Lǐ ‘(He is) not surnamed Li.’, rather than *不姓 bú xìng. When the question is 李先生叫開文嗎？ Lǐ Xiānshēng jiào Kāiwén ma? ‘Is Mr. Li called Kaiwen?’, the negative reply should be 不叫開文 Bú jiào Kāiwén ‘(He is) not called Kaiwen.’, rather than *不叫 bú jiào.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Function: The adverb 很 hěn modifies state verbs (Vs).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 我很好。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他很喜歡臺灣。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 臺灣人很喜歡喝烏龍茶。
items.py: Táiwān rén hěn xǐhuān hē Wūlóng chá.
items.en: Taiwanese people like to drink Oolong tea.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Structures: The adverb 很 hěn is placed before state verbs (Vs) as follows: Subject 很 hěn + State Verb.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 烏龍茶很好喝。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他很喜歡日本人。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 我們很好。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Usage: In general, adjectival state verbs must be preceded by either 不 or intensifiers. When no particular intensity is intended, they are preceded by 很 hěn. That is, 很 hěn + stative verb means ‘very stative verb’ (very expensive, very good, very tall, etc.) and sometimes it just means a stative verb. When 很 is intended to actually mean ‘very’, it is typically stressed in speech.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Function: The 呢 ne question is a tag question with a short form following a statement.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 我要喝茶，你呢？
items.py: Wǒ yào hē chá, nǐ ne?
items.en: I want to drink tea, and you?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他不喝咖啡，陳小姐呢？
items.py: Tā bù hē kāfēi, Chén Xiǎojiě ne?
items.en: He does not drink coffee. What about Miss Chen?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 王先生是日本人，李先生呢？
items.py: Wáng Xiānshēng shì Rìběn rén, Lǐ Xiānshēng ne?
items.en: Mr. Wang is Japanese. What about Mr. Li?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Structures: 1. Same predicate, different subjects — S1 V O, S2 呢 ne?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他是美國人，你呢？
items.py: Tā shì Měiguó rén, nǐ ne?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 他喜歡我們，你呢？
items.en: He likes us. How about you?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: 2. Same subject, different predicates — S V O1, O2 呢 ne?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: “Come over for some tea!” is a common phrase used much like the phrase in English, “You really have to drop by my place sometime for a cup of coffee”. In Taiwan, friends gather around a table with a tea set on it in their free time and drink tea. They drink the tea from delicate, little teacups and might discuss its fragrance and taste. Chatting over tea is a favorite way of the Chinese to bond and keep abreast of the latest things in their lives.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: At home, many people make themselves a cup of hot tea or prepare a pot for the family for after-dinner conversation. Many people like to start off the day at the office with a cup of tea. Those with a more discerning palate might make tea using tea leaves, while teabags probably suffices for others. In the end, they all enjoy a nice cup of hot tea.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: In the shade of old trees in parks or near temples, you can find folks sitting around small tables drinking tea and snacking on melon seeds. Tea is an everyday part of life of the people of Taiwan.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: It is customary for Chinese to call friends and loved ones by nicknames. The character “老” lǎo is sometimes added before the last name or “小” xiǎo placed in front of the second character of the given name to form nicknames. Due to the influence of the Taiwanese dialect, nicknames in Taiwan are often formed by placing the character “阿” ā in front of the name or the second character of the given name is repeated. For example, someone by the name of “陳文華” could be nicknamed “老陳,” “小陳,” “小華,” “華華,” or “阿華.”

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: The tone for 不 bù changes depending on the tone of the character that follows it. When 不 bù is followed by a character with a first, second, or third tone, 不 bù is pronounced and the pinyin marked with a fourth tone (ˋ). When 不 bù is followed by a character with a fourth tone, it is pronounced and the pinyin marked with a second tone (ˊ).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 1 · 歡迎你來臺灣！
items.text: Chinese calligraphy consists of eight basic strokes. These are also the basic strokes of Chinese characters. These eight basic strokes are “horizontal” (橫 héng), “vertical” (豎 shù), “brush left” (撇 piě), “press down and drag” (捺 nà), “dot” (點 diǎn), “flick” (挑 tiǎo), “hook” (鉤 gōu), and “corner fold” (折 zhé). They are used to teach beginners to write Chinese characters.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Structures: Notice that 的 de is sometimes omitted, e.g., 5 & 6 above.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 1. If the relationship between the possessor and the possessed of the two nouns is close, 的 de can be omitted, e.g., 我爸爸 wǒ bàba ‘my dad’, 我哥哥 wǒ gēge ‘my brother’, 我家 wǒ jiā ‘my home’. Furthermore, the possessor has to be a pronoun when 的 de is omitted. So, one can say 李先生的爸爸 Lǐ Xiānshēng de bàba ‘Mr. Li's dad’, but not *李先生爸爸 Lǐ Xiānshēng bàba (omitting 的 de).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 2. If the two nouns in a possessive relationship refer to an individual and his/her affiliated group, the noun referring to the individual usually appears in the plural rather than the singular form. For example, for ‘his home’, it is 他們家 tāmen jiā (their home), 我們日本 wǒmen rìběn (our Japan).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Function: 的 de is used between the modifier and the head noun.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Usage: Notice that 的 de can be omitted when the modifier and the head noun are used together frequently. For example, when talking about nationality, one says 哪國人？ Něi guó rén? ‘person from which country?’, rather than *哪國的人 Něi guó de rén. One says 臺灣人 Táiwān rén ‘Taiwanese people’ rather than *臺灣的人 Táiwān de rén.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Structures: 都 dōu is an adverb, which is placed after the noun it relates to and before the main verb phrase, i.e. Noun + 都 dōu + VP.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Usage:

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 1. 都 dōu is an adverb and appears before the verb and after the subject. It is not correct to say *都我們是臺灣人 Dōu wǒmen shì Táiwān rén.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 2. Members of a group indicated by 都 dōu all have to appear before 都 dōu. For example, to say ‘I like both teachers Li and Wang’, one says 李老師、王老師，我都喜歡。Lǐ Lǎoshī, Wáng Lǎoshī, wǒ dōu xǐhuān. It is incorrect to say *我都喜歡李老師、王老師。 Wǒ dōu xǐhuān Lǐ Lǎoshī, Wáng Lǎoshī.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 3. In interrogatives, 都 dōu works with the 嗎 ma question form but not with A-not-A question forms. For example, to say ‘Are you all surnamed Wang?’, one can say 你們都姓王嗎？ Nǐmen dōu xìng Wáng ma? but not *你們都姓不姓王？ Nǐmen dōu xìng bú xìng Wáng?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 4. When 都 dōu is modified by 不 bù, the sentence means ‘not all....’, e.g., 他們不都是臺灣人。Tāmen bù dōu shì Táiwān rén. ‘Not all of them are Taiwanese’.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Function: Both 個 ge and 張 zhāng are measures. When indicating a quantity, a measure word is placed between the number and the noun.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 一個哥哥

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 兩張好看的照片

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 幾個老師？

items.text: 哪三個人？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 三個人

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 幾張照片？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 哪一張照片？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: When the number following 哪 nǎ is 一 yī ‘one’, the number is often omitted. For example, 哪一個人？ Nǎ yí ge rén? ‘which person?’ is the same as 哪個人？ Něi ge rén?.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Usage:

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 1. There are many measure words in Chinese. Different measure words are used with different nouns. In this lesson, only two measure words are introduced. 個 ge is the most frequently used measure word and is used as the measure for many different nouns. 張 zhāng is usually used with nouns that designate flat objects such as paper, photographs, and tables. When learning a new noun, you need to pay attention to the measure words that can be used with it.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 2. When the numeral is “two”, you do not say “二 èr + measure + noun”, rather you say “兩 liǎng + measure + noun”, e.g., 兩個妹妹 liǎng ge mèimei (two younger sisters), 兩個日本人 liǎng ge Rìběn rén (two Japanese people), 兩張照片 liǎng zhāng zhàopiàn (two photos).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: The family is central to Chinese culture. Chinese parents expect to live with their children, especially their sons. In the past, sons always lived with their parents, even after they were married. Sons would also receive the family inheritance, while the daughters would not. Daughters were considered “members of someone else's family” once they got married, so they did not live with their parents, nor did they receive any inheritance from them.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: In modern society, it is becoming increasingly difficult to find a family with three generations under one roof, but it is still common to find married couples living near their parents/in-laws, sometimes even next door. Being in close proximity allows them to look after each other easily. Since many young Taiwanese couples work, they opt to have their parents look after their children instead of hiring a professional nanny. Having grandparents look after your children saves money and you don't have to worry about leaving your children with a stranger. For their part, the grandparents are generally more than happy to be surrounded by their grandkids.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: More and more people in Taiwan today are also waiting longer to get married. Traditionally, single adults are still children in Chinese culture. As such, many single adults in their 30s and 40s still live with their parents and their parents continue to look after them.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 1. Pinyin Rules: When the vowel “i” stands alone (without a consonant in front of it), it is spelled yī (一). When the vowel “u” stands alone, it is spelled wǔ (五).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: 2. Tone Changes for 一 Yī

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: (1) When 一 is used in names or in ordinal number, its tone does not undergo changes, e.g. Tiánzhōng Chéngyī (田中誠一) and dì yī kè (第一課).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: (2) When 一 yī is used to signify an amount (followed by quantifiers) or when it appears in multisyllabic words, it follows the same tone change rules as 不 bù.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Note: When pronouncing “-o,” it is natural to pronounce it with a slight “u”, as in 伯 b(u)ó, 週末 zhōum(u)ò in Lesson Three, and 微波 wéib(u)ō in Lesson Four.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: To write beautiful Chinese characters, tidiness, balance, symmetry, and harmony are important. Nine-square grids are used to practice writing characters to achieve balanced beauty.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Nine-square grids used for writing practice consist of nine boxes in 3x3 grids. Since Chinese characters can be as simple as “一” or as complicated as “謝”, to achieve balance, symmetry, harmony, and fullness, they must occupy the same amount of space, regardless of how many strokes they have, when written in 3x3 grids.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 2 · 我的家人
items.text: Nine-square grids are a basic tool used for practicing the writing of Chinese characters. Beginners who use the grids to help them layout the structure of Chinese characters will eventually achieve balance in their writing.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Usage: Units of time in a series are expressed from larger to smaller. For example,

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 1. 明天晚上 míngtiān wǎnshàng (tomorrow evening) — not *晚上明天

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 2. 週末早上 zhōumò zǎoshàng (in the morning on the weekend) — not *早上週末

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Function: 去 qù + VP indicates the intention to go do something.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Structures: Negation markers, auxiliary verbs, and adverbs are placed before 去 qù.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Function: When you want to describe, explain, or evaluate a person, event, or thing, you place the person, event, or thing at the beginning of the sentence as the “topic”. The rest of the sentence serves as the “comment”. The topic of a sentence is usually the person or thing that is placed at the beginning of the sentence.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 臺灣人喜歡喝烏龍茶嗎？

items.en: Do Taiwanese people like to drink Oolong tea?

items.text: 烏龍茶，臺灣人都喜歡喝。
items.py: Wūlóng chá, Táiwān rén dōu xǐhuān hē.
items.en: Oolong tea, Taiwanese people all like to drink (it).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 你想看美國電影還是臺灣電影？
items.py: Nǐ xiǎng kàn Měiguó diànyǐng háishì Táiwān diànyǐng?

items.en: American movie, Taiwanese movie, I would like to watch either.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Structures: Topics are always placed at the very beginning of a sentence.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？

items.py: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn, wǒ juéde hěn hǎokàn.
items.en: This photo, I think (it) is quite nice.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Usage: In a topic-comment sentence, if the fronted object consists of a collective noun, or more than one noun, the totality marker, 都 dōu is required.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 中國菜，我都喜歡吃。（collective noun）
items.py: Zhōngguó cài, wǒ dōu xǐhuān chī.
items.en: Chinese food, I like to eat (them) all.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 弟弟、妹妹，我都有。（two object nouns）
items.en: Younger brothers and younger sisters, I've got both.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Structures:

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 1. 也 yě, 都 dōu and 常 cháng are adverbs. Adverbs modify verbs. Adverbs always occur before the verb in Chinese.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 也 yě／都 dōu／常 cháng + VP

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 2. When 也 yě and either 都 dōu or 常 cháng occur in a sentence together to modify the VP, 也 yě is placed before 都 dōu or 常 cháng.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Negation: In negation, 也 yě is placed before the negation markers 不 bù／沒 méi, while 常 cháng is placed after 不 bù. 都 dōu can occur before or after 不 bù, but it changes the meaning of the sentence.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 我不是日本人，他也不是日本人。
items.py: Wǒ bú shì Rìběn rén, tā yě bú shì Rìběn rén.
items.en: I am not Japanese and he is not, either.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 我沒有弟弟，也沒有妹妹。
items.py: Wǒ méi yǒu dìdi, yě méi yǒu mèimei.
items.en: I don't have a younger brother or a younger sister.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 他不喜歡看電影，我也不喜歡看電影。
items.py: Tā bù xǐhuān kàn diànyǐng, wǒ yě bù xǐhuān kàn diànyǐng.
items.en: He doesn't like to watch movies and I don't like to watch movies, either.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 我不常看電影。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 我們都不是美國人。
items.py: Wǒmen dōu bú shì Měiguó rén.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Shrimp fishing is a one-of-a-kind leisure activity found only in Taiwan. It is popular among locals and foreigners living in Taiwan and can be found on many travel itineraries for tourists.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: The shrimp caught at shrimp-fishing sites are raised specifically for that purpose. The facilities are open to the public who is charged by the hour. Shrimp fishing originated in southern Taiwan in the 1980s and gradually spread to the rest of Taiwan. The first venues were outdoors, but shrimp fishing eventually became an indoor activity as enthusiasts wanted to stay out of the sun and weather. An indoor shrimp-fishing facility is a great place to spend half a day. You can roast the shrimp you catch or have them roasted by the staff and eat them right there.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: There are many ways to cook shrimp, but nothing beats eating roasted shrimp and drinking beer. This laid-back leisure activity is a good way to relieve stress and a great escape from the hustle and bustle of daily life.

items.text: Pinyin Rules

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: When the vowel “ü” is preceded by the consonant “j”, “q”, or “x,” the umlaut (the two dots above the letter) is omitted, e.g., jué (覺). When it is not preceded by any consonant, it is spelled yù (玉).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: When the vowel “i” is followed by the vowel “a”, “o”, or “e” and is not preceded by consonant, change the “i” to a “y”, e.g., -iao → yào (要), -ie → yě (也).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Learning Chinese characters requires familiarizing yourself with their pronunciations, meanings, and form. The form (structure of Chinese characters) consists of structures with three tiers: the entire character itself, components, and strokes.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Components are the basic units of Chinese characters

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Components are the smallest writing unit to Chinese characters. They fall between strokes and radicals (strokes ≦ components ≦ radicals) and are the core structures of Chinese writing. Independent characters have only one component and compound characters have at least two components. For example, the character in “好” has two components: “女” and “子.”

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 好＝女＋子

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: The character “樂” (happy) has three components: “白,” “幺,” and “木.”

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: 樂＝白＋幺＋幺＋木

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: The most effective way to learn characters

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 3 · 週末做什麼？
items.text: Using components to learn Chinese characters helps the learner break down the complicated forms of characters and makes learning easier. Components also help the learner understand characteristics of Chinese characters and speeds up word recognition and learning, while helping build up word repertoire.

items.text: Function: 太 tài…了 le indicates “too” or “overly”, a negative observation given by the speaker.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: Usage:

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: 1. “太 tài + Vs” means that a noun is “too” or “overly” (adj.). This pattern can also be used as a predicate, e.g., 那支手機太貴。Nà zhī shǒujī tài guì. ‘That cell phone is too expensive’.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: 2. “太 tài + Vs + 了” is more subjective, indicating that the speaker feels that what is being talked about is excessively (adj.). For example, 那支手機太貴了。Nà zhī shǒujī tài guì le. ‘That cell phone is way too expensive’.

items.text: Students who are new to Taiwan can buy their meals without knowing a single word in Chinese. They can do this in any of Taiwan's 24/7 convenience stores. Many students will probably even miss the convenience of these stores after they have returned to their countries and wish that they could take the stores home with them.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: Convenience stores are very important to local life in Taiwan and offer an impressive range of services. You get full meals, snacks, drinks, stationary supplies, articles for daily use, DVDs, fashion magazines, and newspapers as well as make photocopies, fax documents, withdraw money, pay bills, and even mail letters and packages at convenience stores. What's more, you can pick up merchandise, books, and tickets that you order online. During holidays, you can place orders for a festive meal or a cake at a convenience store and then pick it up anytime.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: 1. Pinyin Rules

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: When “zh-”, “ch-”, and “sh-” stand alone, an “i” is added to the end. When “-iao” does not follow a consonant, change the “i” to “y” to form yào（要）(see Lesson Three for explanations).

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: When the vowel “u” is followed by other vowels, but is not preceded by a consonant, change the “u” to “w,” as in “u” + “ei” → wéi（微）. However, when “u + ei” is preceded by a consonant, the “e” is omitted and the spelling becomes “ui,” as in duì（對）and guì（貴）. The pronunciation, however, remains “du(e)i.”

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: 2. Tone Mark Rules (Position of the Tone Marks)

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: All tone marks in pinyin are placed above the vowels, as in bà（爸）, mā（媽）, bó（伯）, and mǔ（母）. Please note that when placing the tone mark above “i,” the dot is not necessary, as in yī（一）. With compound vowels, the placement of tone marks is prioritized as follows: a > e, o > i, u, ü.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: Example: lái（來）, zhào（照）, měi（美）, jué（覺）, dōu（都）, xiǎo（小）. Also note that a/e, e/o never appear together.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: When “i” and “u” appear together, the tone mark is placed above the last appearing vowel, as in duì（對）, niú（牛）.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 4 · 請問一共多少錢？
items.text: Radicals are components of Chinese characters, usually on the left, that systematically categorize Chinese characters by their meanings. For example, eating “吃” and drinking “喝” require the use of the mouth, thus they fall under the mouth “口” radical; listening “聽” requires the use of one's ears, hence naturally belongs to the ear “耳” radical. Radicals lend hand to the cognition and memory of Chinese characters, and lead to the understanding of the characters' fundamental meanings. When learners do not know the pronunciation of a certain character, they can use their knowledge of radicals to look up the character. There are 214 radicals in used in modern day dictionaries, below are 35 commonly used ones from words you have already learned thus far.

items.text: Structures: Since this expression suggests negative evaluation, there is no negative form for the pattern. If the Vs has a positive meaning, it can’t be used in this pattern. For example, one can say, 這張照片有一點舊。Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn yǒu yìdiǎn jiù. ‘This photo is a little old’. However, you cannot say *他妹妹有一點漂亮 Tā mèimei yǒu yìdiǎn piàoliàng. ‘His younger sister is a little beautiful’.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Function: The complement marker 得 de follows the verb and introduces the complement, which describes the result or state of the action suggested by the verb.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他學中文學得不錯。
items.py: Tā xué Zhōngwén xué de búcuò.
items.en: He has learned Chinese quite well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 王伯母做越南菜做得很好。
items.py: Wáng Bómǔ zuò Yuènán cài zuò de hěn hǎo.
items.en: Auntie Wang cooks Vietnamese food very well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 你做得很好。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 這種手機賣得很好。
items.py: Zhè zhǒng shǒujī mài de hěn hǎo.
items.en: This type of cell phone sells well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Structures: When a complement is added to a transitive verb, several structural consequences follow.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 1. When its object directly follows the verb, the verb is repeated before 得 de and the complement.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 你做飯做得真好吃。
items.py: Nǐ zuòfàn zuò de zhēn hǎochī.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 我的老師教中文教得很好。
items.py: Wǒ de lǎoshī jiāo Zhōngwén jiāo de hěn hǎo.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 2. When the object appears at the front of the sentence, the verb is not repeated.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 飯，他做得真好吃。
items.py: Fàn, tā zuò de zhēn hǎochī.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 中文，你說得很好。
items.py: Zhōngwén, nǐ shuō de hěn hǎo.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 這種甜點，他做得很好吃。
items.py: Zhè zhǒng tiándiǎn, tā zuò de hěn hǎochī.
items.en: He makes this kind of dessert very tasty.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 這支手機賣得很便宜。
items.py: Zhè zhī shǒujī mài de hěn piányí.
items.en: This cell phone is sold cheaply.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Negation: Negation occurs only within the complement.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他做甜點做得不好。
items.py: Tā zuò tiándiǎn zuò de bù hǎo.
items.en: He does not make desserts well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 王先生打網球打得不好。
items.py: Wáng Xiānshēng dǎ wǎngqiú dǎ de bù hǎo.
items.en: Mr. Wang does not play the tennis well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他的咖啡賣得不好。
items.py: Tā de kāfēi mài de bù hǎo.
items.en: His coffee does not sell well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 越南菜，這家店做得不好吃。
items.py: Yuènán cài, zhè jiā diàn zuò de bù hǎochī.
items.en: This shop does not cook Vietnamese food well.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他做飯做得怎麼樣？

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他打籃球打得好嗎？
items.py: Tā dǎ lánqiú dǎ de hǎo ma?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 中文，他說得好不好？
items.py: Zhōngwén, tā shuō de hǎo bù hǎo?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Function: 會 huì indicates that these skills are acquired through learning.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 陳小姐會做飯。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他哥哥會踢足球。
items.en: His older brother knows how to play soccer.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他們兄弟姐妹都會游泳。
items.py: Tāmen xiōngdì jiěmèi dōu huì yóuyǒng.
items.en: All of those siblings know how to swim.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Structures: 會 huì is an auxiliary verb and can be negated.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他的媽媽不會做飯。
items.py: Tā de māma bú huì zuòfàn.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 我媽媽不會做甜點。
items.py: Wǒ māma bú huì zuò tiándiǎn.
items.en: My mom does not know how to make desserts.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 我的家人都不會打棒球。
items.py: Wǒ de jiārén dōu bú huì dǎ bàngqiú.
items.en: None of the members of my family knows how to play baseball.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 你會做甜點嗎？
items.en: Do you know how to make desserts?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他弟弟會踢足球嗎？
items.py: Tā dìdi huì tī zúqiú ma?
items.en: Does his younger brother know how to play football?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 你會不會說中文？
items.py: Nǐ huì bú huì shuō Zhōngwén?
items.en: Do you know how to speak Chinese?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 你的姐姐會不會做飯？
items.py: Nǐ de jiějie huì bú huì zuòfàn?
items.en: Does your elder sister know how to cook?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Function: The preposition 到 dào indicates the destination of a movement.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他這個週末到臺灣來。
items.py: Tā zhè ge zhōumò dào Táiwān lái.
items.en: He is coming to Taiwan this weekend.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 老師明天到臺北來。我們要和他一起吃晚飯。
items.py: Lǎoshī míngtiān dào Táiběi lái. Wǒmen yào hàn tā yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
items.en: The teacher is coming to Taipei tomorrow. We are having dinner with him.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 想吃牛肉麵嗎？明天我們可以到那家店去。
items.py: Xiǎng chī niúròu miàn ma? Míngtiān wǒmen kěyǐ dào nà jiā diàn qù.
items.en: Would you like to have beef noodles? We can go to that shop tomorrow.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 我可以教你中文，明天到我家來吧！
items.py: Wǒ kěyǐ jiāo nǐ Zhōngwén, míngtiān dào wǒ jiā lái ba!
items.en: I can teach you Chinese. Go ahead and come to my house tomorrow.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Structures:

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Negation: Negation is always done by placing a negator in front of a preposition, not the main verb.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 王先生明天不到臺北來。
items.py: Wáng Xiānshēng míngtiān bú dào Táiběi lái.
items.en: Mr. Wang is not coming to Taipei tomorrow.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 那家的越南菜不好吃。他們不到那家餐廳去。
items.py: Nà jiā de Yuènán cài bù hǎochī. Tāmen bú dào nà jiā cāntīng qù.
items.en: That shop’s Vietnamese food doesn’t taste good. They don’t go to that restaurant.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他晚上去看電影，不到我家來，你呢？
items.py: Tā wǎnshàng qù kàn diànyǐng, bú dào wǒ jiā lái, nǐ ne?
items.en: He is going to go to a movie tonight and will not be coming to my house. How about you?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Questions: 到 dào can be used to form A-not-A questions.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 你妹妹到不到臺灣來？
items.py: Nǐ mèimei dào bú dào Táiwān lái?
items.en: Is your younger sister coming to Taiwan?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他們到不到我家來？
items.py: Tāmen dào bú dào wǒ jiā lái?
items.en: Are they coming to my house?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Usage: The destination marker 到 dào is a preposition and another verb serves as the main verb in the sentence (e.g., 來 lái ‘come’ or 去 qù ‘go’). In Taiwan and Southern China, however, 到 dào is often used as a verb, like 來 lái or 去 qù.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 這麼多家餐廳，我們要到哪一家？
items.py: Zhème duō jiā cāntīng, wǒmen yào dào nǎ yì jiā?
items.en: There are so many restaurants. Which one should we go?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 他們明天晚上要到王老師家。你想去嗎？
items.py: Tāmen míngtiān wǎnshàng yào dào Wáng lǎoshī jiā. Nǐ xiǎng qù ma?
items.en: They are going to Teacher Wang’s house tomorrow evening. Would you like to go?

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 歡迎你到我家。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Goal: Learning the names of common foods and how to read them.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Task: Compete with classmates to see who can name the most street foods. Find pictures of food you know and bring them to class. Show each picture and say the name of the food it shows.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Goal: Learning to make simple comments about common objects.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Task: Read the following statements, then make comments on the statements using 很, 太 or 有一點.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Example

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 一碗牛肉麵一百八十塊錢。
items.py: Yì wǎn niúròu miàn yìbǎi bāshí kuài qián.
items.en: A bowl of beef noodles costs NT$180.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 有一點貴。

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Goal: Learning to describe what someone can/can’t do and how well s/he does it.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Task: There is going to be a talent contest at school. Find out what your classmates can do and how well they can do it. Record your findings. Ask questions using phrases that you learned, like 做甜點、游泳、照相、打籃球、踢足球、做小籠包、打網球. (Make desserts, swim, take pictures, play basketball, play soccer, make xiaolongbao, play tennis.)

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Goal: Learning to ask for help.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Task: From the survey you completed in Task III, find one item that interests you and ask the person if s/he could teach you how do to it, e.g., 我想學做小籠包，你可以教我嗎？(I want to learn how to make xiaolongbao. Can you teach me?)

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Lines in front of roadside food stands are a familiar scene in Taiwan. Food stalls usually open for business at fixed times and in fixed locations. As long as the food sold at a stall is fresh, inexpensive, and good, you can be sure there will be a long queue in front of it regardless of the weather.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: With a little pocket change, you can buy delicious baozi, scallion pancakes, wheel-barrel cakes, or pan-fried dumplings. It is little wonder that there are queues on almost every street corner.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Street vendors are very common in Taiwan. They are the product of farmer’s markets and temple festivals of an agricultural society of a time passed. Today, street vendors are seen in scenic sites, residential areas, outskirts of markets, business district surroundings, on arcaded corridors, on the streets, outside examination sites, and during temple festivals. The selections of vendors range from daily goods to food to souvenirs. Since street vendors are very mobile, they sometimes affect traffic, disturb quiet neighborhoods, or scar cityscape. If street vendors could be regulated, they could add to the excitement and beauty of the city.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Pinyin Rules

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: As with “zh-/zhi,” “ch-/chi,” and “sh-/shi,” when “z-,” “c-,” and “s-” stand alone, “i” is added to form zi, ci, and si.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: When “u” is followed by other vowels, but is not preceded by a consonant, change the “u” to “w,” as in “u” + “ei” → wéi 微 in Lesson Four and “u” + “o” → wǒ 我 in Lesson 1.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: When the vowel “i” is followed by “ou” but is not preceded by a consonant, change the “i” to “y” to form 有 yǒu (Refer to Lesson 2). When a consonant precedes the “i” + “ou” compound, the “o” is omitted and it becomes “-iu,” e.g., 牛 → niú, 六 → liù. The “o,” however, is still pronounced, e.g., → “ni(o)ú” and “li(o)ù.”

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: There are three general beliefs regarding the origin of Chinese characters:

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 1. Chinese characters were created by a person by the name of Cangjie.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 2. Chinese characters originated from the eight trigrams and rope-knotting.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: 3. Chinese characters originated from pictograms. This is also the most widely adopted belief among scholars.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: Characters were not created by any single person, at any single time, or at any specific place. They were developed and accumulated over time. Most scholars believe that Chinese characters originated from pictures or drawings and slowly became signs and characters.

items.title: A1 Textbook · Pelajaran 5 · 牛肉麵真好吃
items.text: The Chinese characters we see and use today have undergone many thousands of years of evolution, from the oracle bone script of the Shang Dynasty to bronze script and Large Seal script of the Zhou Dynasty to the Small Seal script that was adopted after the Qin Dynasty and used to unite the Six Kingdoms. These scripts are classified as ancient scripts. During the Han Dynasty, the symmetrical and rounded look of Small Seal script was modified to become more rectangular and orderly, making writing easier and faster. This came to known as Clerical script. The Regular script we use now evolved directly from the Clerical script. In other words, the standardized characters in use today were shaped and formed during the Han Dynasty.

items.title: Band A Reading · Series 1 · Soal 46
items.text: （一） 曾有一項調查發現，很多員工生病的時候不敢請假，因為他們擔心老闆會不高興，覺得他們沒有責任感。有人認為，員工會這麼想是公司的責任。一個好的公司應該能照顧員工，而不是讓他們拿健康去換錢。因此，讓員工有幸福感，應該是未來企業努力的方向。 這篇文章說了什麼內容？ 老闆應該給員工多一點兒假 常關心別人的人更有責任感 對公司有意見要勇敢說出來 照顧身體比認真工作更重要

items.title: Band A Reading · Series 1 · Soal 47
items.text: （二） 如果你每天都覺得身體很累，有一份報告或許可以告訴你原因。這份報告提到了下面幾種可能：不愛運動、水喝得不夠多、總是把事情想得太壞、不吃早餐、吃太多沒營養的食物等。以上幾點，只要簡單思考一下自己符合了幾項，再試著做出一些改變，想讓自己更健康一點也不難。 在改善健康方面，下面哪一個是作者的建議？ 要培養運動的好習慣 想要吃什麼就吃什麼 平常應該多做點好事 吃早餐以後不要喝水

items.title: Band A Reading · Series 1 · Soal 48
items.text: （三） 從前有一個地方很久都不下雨，人們不管怎麼求雨都沒有用。有一次，他們從很遠的地方，請來一位有智慧的老人，希望他可以幫幫忙。老人在附近走了走、看了看，然後告訴他們，請蓋一間小屋，讓他住進去三天，三天當中，他任何人都不見。結果，三天後真的下雨了。大家都問他是怎麼做到的，他只回答，只要自己的心安靜了，外面就安靜了，所以下雨了。 這個故事告訴了我們什麼事？ 先照顧自己，才能幫助別人 想改變環境，就先改變心情 年輕人應該要學會尊敬老人 聰明的人知道什麼時候下雨

items.title: Band A Reading · Series 1 · Soal 49
items.text: （四） 說到錢，每個人對它的想法、使用方式和重視程度都不一樣。有人說：「錢是沒有性格的，它在誰的手上就像誰」。這句話說得很有道理，人們因為對錢的看法不同，而選擇不同的生活方式。比方說，有的人喜歡看到銀行裡的數字不斷增加，所以每天努力工作，很少花錢；有的人覺得錢只要夠用就好，不必太在意工作，因為「自己的時間」，也是一種看不到的「錢」。 這段話說了下面哪件事？ 錢比什麼都重要 錢可以解決所有事情 人人有自己對錢的看法 錢得放在銀行裡才有價值

items.title: Band A Reading · Series 1 · Soal 50
items.text: （五） 以前，電影院的門口常常出現一個牌子，要觀眾別帶外面買的食物進去，如果想吃東西，只能買電影院裡賣的食物。後來，新聞說，觀眾其實可以拒絕配合這些電影院的規矩。說到這個問題，我認為，電影院的要求不是沒有道理，因為電影結束以後，他們還得打掃那些垃圾。其次，如果有人帶了一些有奇怪味道的食物進電影院，也很容易影響其他看電影的人。 作者對在電影院裡吃東西的行為怎麼看？ 應該要避免吃有特別味道的東西 覺得吃什麼東西都是個人的自由 認為電影院的要求沒有任何道理 看電影的人都有責任要打掃垃圾

items.text: （四） 一項研究發現，女人比男人更容易感覺到「疼痛」，也就是說，在相同的情況下，女人對痛的感覺比男人高出 20%。研究還發現，聽音樂可有效降低疼痛感。換句話說，因牙齒痛去看牙時，可以聽音樂或玩一些帶有音樂的遊戲。好聽的、有趣的音樂不但能讓你覺得沒那麼痛，也能幫助你別太注意旁邊機器的聲音。 這個研究說了什麼？ 女人在音樂方面的興趣與表現比男人高得多 聽音樂的時候，人們比較不容易感覺到疼痛 看病時播放音樂，有助於降低醫院內的噪音 男人比女人更怕痛，牙痛時常不願去看牙醫

items.text: （五） 一位二十歲的大學生，花了一年的時間，製造出了一台煮咖啡的機器。這台咖啡機能讓人只用「嘴」就煮出咖啡！如果你是這台咖啡機的主人，想喝咖啡的時候，只需要在離它三公尺以內的地方說：「煮一杯熱咖啡！」。大概五分鐘以後，你就能夠喝到一杯熱熱的咖啡。 根據這段介紹，可以知道什麼事？ 咖啡機是透過聲音來控制的 咖啡的品質不能只用嘴來判斷 第一個發明咖啡機的是個年輕人 用這台咖啡機煮咖啡，多遠都聞得到

items.title: Band B Reading · Series 2 · Soal 21
items.text: （六） 西洋情人節這一天，情人之間會互相贈送禮物，主要是希望能向對方表達自己濃濃的愛。送給情人的禮物有很多選擇，其中，除了常見的鮮花，巧克力也是很受歡迎的禮物。有些人覺得巧克力太甜，容易讓人變胖。事實上，每天吃一點巧克力對健康很有幫助，尤其是顏色深、味道苦的巧克力，越黑越苦越健康。 關於這篇文章，下面哪一個是正確的？ 深色巧克力不比淺色的健康 現代人早已不流行買花、送花 吃巧克力不是對身體沒有好處 情人節送禮物才能證明彼此的愛

items.title: Band B Reading · Series 2 · Soal 22
items.text: （七） 一般人都以為用 CD 儲存資料，就能永久保存珍貴的相片或影片，這恐怕是錯誤觀念。日本最新研究發現，CD 也有壽命，如果 CD長期被放在潮濕的地方或陽光下，時間久了，檔案損壞的風險一定較高。因此，要想保存珍貴影像，最好還是定期在不同地方多儲存幾份。 這篇文章談到關於使用 CD 存檔的哪一件事？ 是最能保障檔案品質的方式 所儲存的內容都有保存期限 其壽命比一般人想像的還長 存檔程序複雜是唯一的缺點

items.text: （八） 在中國，多數人長久以來都認為紙是東漢時期的蔡倫發明的，如今這個觀點被推翻了。根據考古學家的最新發現，在蔡倫之前，中國人早已知道如何造紙，只是造紙的品質較差罷了。儘管蔡倫不是發明紙的人，但他卻改進了造紙的材料和技術。大家為了紀念他的貢獻，便把這種改良過的紙叫做「蔡侯紙」。 根據這段話，下面哪一項是對的？ 考古學家不贊同蔡倫擅長造紙 「蔡侯紙」是中國人最早發明的紙 很多人最近才知道東漢以前沒有紙 蔡倫的主要成就在於改進造紙的品質

items.text: （七） 一般大眾常覺得每天都吃早餐的人比較聰明，檢視 1950 年到2008 年之間的相關研究後發現，吃早餐似乎只對經濟狀況較差的學生在學業表現上有幫助，而理由恐怕不是因為身體在早上需要營養。主要是貧窮孩子被當時學校供應的免費麵包和牛奶給吸引，才乖乖來上課。2014 年，荷蘭一群研究者設計了一個實驗，他們發現參與實驗的 30 位大學生在沒吃早餐的情況下，測驗的成績較為突出。 心理學家卡斯楚也發表過很多關於早餐的論文，他認為吃較多的早餐能讓肥胖者午、晚餐吃得較少，最後達成瘦身的目的。但康乃爾大學的研究指出，早上吃很多的人，並不會減少吃午飯的量，經過仔細的計算，一天下來吃進肚子裡的食物總量反而增加。 究竟是吃早餐好？還是不吃早餐好呢？我覺得，餓了就吃最自然。 根據本文，為什麼吃早餐對貧窮孩子的學業表現有幫助？ 早餐讓他們的身體變得健康 早餐讓他們比較有上學的意願 學校提供的麵包牛奶對頭腦很好

items.title: Band B Reading · Series 5 · Soal 41
items.text: （十二） 在某些社會文化中，由於「一個人吃飯」通常與被孤立、沒朋友、不懂社交等負面印象聯繫在一起，所以一個人走進餐廳就成了許多人害怕的事。但，獨自吃飯真是一件那麼糟糕的事嗎？ 事實上，一個人並不意味著寂寞，與此相反，更可以將注意力放在享受餐盤上的美食。當然，與他人分享、交流時能帶給人們滿足與快樂，而當你已經在人際相處上付出了許多時間後，更應該為自己保留一些獨處的空間；當你因為獨自吃飯而害怕被貼上「人際障礙」的標籤時，也許根本沒有人注意到你，或是覺得你性格古怪。 忙碌的生活常常讓我們忽略與自己獨處的重要性，哪怕是一頓飯、一部電影的時間，都是面對自己的好機會。久而久之，你將發現，那些異樣眼光只是一種自我限制，而能一個人吃飯，竟然是那麼寶貴。 作者認為有些人害怕一個人吃飯的原因是什麼？ 不敢違反社交規定 太在意別人的想法 不能分享最新的消息 擔心錯過朋友的邀請

items.title: Band B Reading · Series 5 · Soal 44
items.text: （十三） 在商業活動中，與他人見面交流時，第一步常是交換名片。只是拿到這麼多名片，一方面容易遺失，一方面經過長時間，名片都可以堆成小山了，不只查找不便，也浪費很多空間。 好在電子時代來臨，現在很多人已經選擇使用電子名片。初次見面的時候，雙方可以打開彼此手機裡的電子名片程式，利用自動輸入功能交換彼此的資料。除了可以快速輸入與查找資料外，還能連結手機裡的電話、電子郵件與地圖。和傳統名片不同的是，它能隨時更新資料和照片，不需要換名片，減少了製作名片的材料和成本。只可惜，目前在一些網路不發達的區域，無法隨意使用電子名片，而且要讓不同的名片程式能夠相互交換資料是有困難的。如果要讓電子名片更普遍，仍然需要政府協助建設網路，以及民間企業的配合才行。 作者覺得使用傳統名片的缺點是什麼？ 交換時常浪費不少時間 其材質容易弄髒不耐用 收到太多名片很難找資料 年輕人很少使用傳統名片

items.text: （五） 最近常在電視、報紙上看到類似的新聞：有外籍人士來台旅遊，不小心遺失了巨額旅費，幸好總有熱心的司機、路人將撿到的錢物歸原主，讓外國旅客豎起大拇指，大讚台灣民眾的誠實。 這樣的新聞雖然能對社會產生正面的影響，但也不得不讓人進一步思量：拾金不昧的消息屢屢登上新聞版面，是不是也代表這類行為已經不再被人們視為理所當然？換句話說，在現今社會中，撿到別人遺失的金錢、物品而據為己有的人也不在少數。如此看來，看到這類新聞，我們實在不用太高興。如果有那麼一天，拾金不昧不再是新聞，而那些不願物歸原主、愛占人便宜的人，反而登上新聞版面，這才代表拾金不昧已經成為我們社會裡自然流露的美德。 作者認為，這類新聞反映出社會出現了什麼狀況？ 大家都能做到拾金不昧 大家不認為拾金不昧是美德 大家太過重視拾金不昧的行為 能做到拾金不昧的人其實不多
